message.content:
**Answer**

The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
Laurasiatheria is one of the major branches of placental mammals (Eutheria) and includes the orders Carnivora (cats, dogs, bears, etc.) and Perissodactyla (horses, rhinos, tapirs), among others. The ancestor of Laurasiatheria was a small, probably insectivorous mammal that lived roughly 90 million years ago, before the lineages that led to modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates diverged.
